newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea April M2 supply rise highest in 43 months.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea April M2 supply rise highest in 43 months.

text.p: South Korea's M2 money supply rose 20.8 percent year-on-year in April, the highest in 43 months, against a 14.0 percent rise a year earlier, provisional Bank of Korea (BOK) figures showed on Tuesday.
Note - M2 consists of money in circulation, and checking and savings account deposits with banks. MCT includes banks' trust account savings and certificates of deposit on top of M2.
A central bank official said the M2 rise in April was higher than a year earlier because of a deposit shift in banks from trust accounts to savings accounts.
He said the pace of money flowing into trust accounts had slowed since May 1996, when the maturity was extended up to 18 months from one year.

Deposits in trust accounts increased by only 890 billion won in April, compared with a 4.47 trillion won rise a year ago, he said. But money in savings accounts rose by 2.1 trillion won against 1.12 trillion won.
The official said the money supply measured in MCT fell in April, reflecting stability in the money market.
He said fewer net issues of certificates of deposit (CDs) also contributed to the MCT fall.
Issues of CDs were 192.3 billion won higher than repayments in April. A year ago, CD issues outstripped repayments by 518.5 billion won.
